title: Review: Homologous series; IUPAC nomenclature; Formulae and functional groups; Stereoisomerism (E/Z and optical)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR02#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR02#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR05#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR01#N.5, OR02#N.7, OR03#N.10, OR05#N.14a, OR01#N.9, OR02#N.9, OR03#N.7, OR05#N.12, OR01#N.11, OR02#N.4, OR03#N.11, OR05#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: General formula
items.clue: A single algebraic expression that fits every member of a family of compounds.

items.label: Locant
items.clue: A carbon number within a name, such as the 2 and the 3 in 2-methylpentan-3-ol.

items.label: Functional group
items.clue: The feature shared by every member of a family, giving similar chemical properties.

items.label: Stereoisomers
items.clue: Compounds with one structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol has the molecular formula C₃H₈O. Which statement about the formula C₃H₈O is correct?

options.text: It is the molecular formula only, since an empirical formula is simpler.
It is a structural formula, as it lists every atom present.
It identifies propan-2-ol, since no other compound has this formula.
It is both the molecular and the empirical formula of propan-2-ol.

questions.explanation: 3, 8 and 1 have no common factor, so the ratio is already the simplest. Empirical = molecular here.

questions.stem: The boiling points of four successive alcohols are: methanol 65 °C, ethanol 78 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C and butan-1-ol 118 °C. Which statement explains this trend?

options.text: Longer molecules have more H atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Longer molecules contain more covalent bonds to break on boiling.
Heavier molecules need more energy to move, whatever the forces.
Induced dipole–dipole forces grow with chain length; each has one –OH.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding per molecule stays about the same. Each extra CH₂ adds electrons and contact area, so the induced dipole–dipole forces grow.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?

options.text: 2-methylhexan-4-one
5-methylhexan-3-one
5-methylhexan-3-al
5,5-dimethylpentan-3-one

questions.explanation: Six-carbon chain. From the left, the C=O is on C3 (from the right, C4) and the methyl on C5.

questions.stem: Ibuprofen has one chiral centre. Tablets usually contain a racemic mixture, yet almost all the pain relief comes from one enantiomer, which blocks an enzyme involved in pain and swelling. Which explains why the two enantiomers act differently in the body?

options.text: The enzyme's active site is chiral, so only one enantiomer fits it.
The two enantiomers have different melting points, so one dissolves more slowly in the body.
One enantiomer is the E isomer and the other is the Z isomer of the same structure.
The racemic mixture rotates plane-polarised light, and this deactivates one of the enantiomers.

questions.explanation: The active site is built from chiral amino acids, so it is stereospecific: one enantiomer fits. Same idea as your nose.

questions.stem: Which compound contains an ester group?

options.text: CH₃COOH
CH₃CH₂OCH₃
CH₃COOCH₃
CH₃COCH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: The C=O carbon is bonded to an O that is bonded to a carbon: –COO–. This is methyl ethanoate, an ester.

questions.stem: Butane, C₄H₁₀, boils at −1 °C and is sold as camping gas. Dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆, boils at 216 °C and is a liquid in diesel fuel. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Dodecane molecules contain more C–C and C–H bonds, which must break before it can boil.
Dodecane molecules contain more hydrogen atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Butane and dodecane belong to different homologous series, so their properties differ.
Dodecane chains are longer, so the induced dipole–dipole forces are stronger.

questions.explanation: Longer chains have more electrons and more contact, so the forces between molecules are stronger. More energy is needed to separate them.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO?

options.text: 3-methylbutanal
2-methylbutanol
2-methylbutanal
2-ethylpropanal

questions.explanation: Four-carbon chain including the –CHO carbon, which is C1. The methyl is on C2.

questions.stem: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid made in the laboratory from non-chiral starting materials is a racemic mixture. Which statement about this sample is correct?

options.text: Its molecules are achiral, which is why it does not rotate plane-polarised light.
It holds equal amounts of both enantiomers, whose rotations cancel.
It contains equal amounts of the E and Z isomers.
Fractional distillation separates it into its two enantiomers.

questions.explanation: Each enantiomer rotates the plane by the same angle in opposite directions. In a 1 : 1 mixture the effects cancel.

questions.stem: Two bottles both contain a liquid with the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. Liquid X boils at 118 °C and turns blue litmus red. Liquid Y boils at 32 °C and is neutral. Which explains this?

options.text: X and Y must be the same compound, so one of the two samples must be impure.
X's molecules are heavier, so more energy is needed to separate them.
X is CH₃COOH, with a carboxyl group; Y is HCOOCH₃, with an ester group.
X is CH₃COOH, a carboxylic acid; Y is CH₃CHO, an aldehyde with no acidic O–H group.

questions.explanation: Same atoms, different structures. X's carboxyl O–H makes it acidic and lets its molecules hydrogen-bond, so it boils far higher. The ester has no O–H.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are successive members of the same homologous series?

options.text: CH₃CH₂CHO and CH₃COCH₂CH₃
CH₃COOH and CH₃CH₂COOH
CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl and CH₃CHClCH₃
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH=CHCH₃

questions.explanation: Both are carboxylic acids (CₙH₂ₙO₂) and they differ by one CH₂: ethanoic acid and propanoic acid.

options.text: CH₃CH(CH₃)COCH₂CH₃
CH₃COCH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃
CH₃CH(OH)CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃
CH₃COCH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: pent: five-carbon chain. -2-one: C=O on C2. 3-methyl: a CH₃ branch on C3.

questions.stem: Which carbon atom in 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is a chiral centre?

options.text: C2
C4
C3
None, as every group on C3 starts with a carbon atom.

questions.explanation: C3 carries H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and CH₂CH₂CH₃: four different groups.
